lina: FYI ran into a nasty edge case in the Python quickstart: cancelling an async SSE stream sometimes leaves the process alive. Quick repro below.

josh: Can you drop the minimal repro?

lina: Server: FastAPI + sse-starlette that yields every 0.2s. Client: httpx AsyncClient stream + `async for chunk in r.aiter_bytes():` then break on a condition (or ctrl-c). After breaking the loop the script hangs.

aaron: Typical cause: the background reader task in httpx isn't cancelled automatically when the iterator is abandoned. Did you `await r.aclose()`?

lina: I tried adding `await r.aclose()` in finally and that fixed my local runs. But we ship the naive pattern in quickstart which will hit users. Also saw stacktrace showing `httpx._content._aiter_bytes.<locals>.wrapper` pending on `gen.__anext__()` coming from sse-starlette's sleep.

josh: Two action items: update the sample to call `await r.aclose()` in finally + add a short note about streaming cancellation; and open an SDK ticket to explore whether our wrapper should cancel reader tasks when the iterator is garbage-collected or on iterator exit.

lina: I'll do the samples PR. For the SDK issue I think we should also add a unit test simulating ctrl-c to avoid regressions.

infra-bot: ci: created issue SDK-672 (label: dx, streaming).

aaron: Also recommend server-side improvement: check `if await request.is_disconnected(): break` inside generator so server stops producing sooner when client disconnects. That reduces chance of stuck readers.

lina: Added both changes to my samples PR and updated quickstart docs. Leaving this thread in case anyone wants to pick the SDK investigation. Thanks! :thumbsup:
